reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend helpers, but implements daily occurrence handling separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange.

duplication.why: Nonbusiness-day classification, daily skip decisions, and forward/reverse occurrence filtering repeat instead of sharing one policy.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared schedules, but the server range handler also owns recurrence policy that belongs alongside the shared date logic.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their configuration plumbing, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate daily skip policy across separate enumeration paths, while caller-computed flags prevent the shared weekend abstraction from owning the complete decision.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange locally decides daily skipping and disables applyWeekendRule through skipWeekend && !isDaily, paralleling getNextDate rather than sharing its occurrence policy.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange expresses the daily nonbusiness-day filtering from getNextDate as a flatMap early return, disguising the same policy in a different enumeration shape.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains the holidays option; getNextDate adds a daily-specific take selection and two daily filtering branches; getDatesInRange independently implements the daily policy.
